requirements.heading: Header Fields
requirements.text: Each of these header fields MUST NOT occur more than once in an article.

requirements.heading: Header Fields
requirements.text: Implementations SHOULD NOT use the hash algorithms "sha224" and "sha384" to generate <scheme>.

requirements.heading: Cancel-Lock
requirements.text: Comments in CFWS (comments and/or folding whitespace) can cause interoperability problems, so comments SHOULD NOT be generated but MUST be accepted.

requirements.heading: Cancel-Lock
requirements.text: If <scheme> is not supported by an implementation, the corresponding <c-lock> element MUST be skipped and potential following <c-lock> elements MUST NOT be ignored.

requirements.heading: Cancel-Key
requirements.text: Comments in CFWS can cause interoperability problems, so comments SHOULD NOT be generated but MUST be accepted.

requirements.heading: Cancel-Key
requirements.text: If <scheme> is not supported by an implementation, the corresponding <c-key> element MUST be skipped and potential following <c-key> elements MUST NOT be ignored.

requirements.heading: Cancel-Key
requirements.text: Compliant implementations SHOULD generate valid Base64 (that is to say the syntax of <c-lock-string> as defined in Section 2.1 of this document) and MUST accept strings of <base64-octet> characters (that is to say the syntax of <obs-c-key-string> as defined in Section 6 of this document).

requirements.heading: Adding an Initial Cancel-Lock Header Field to a Proto-Article
requirements.text: A Cancel-Lock header field MAY be added to a proto-article by the poster or posting agent and will include one or more <c-lock> elements.

requirements.heading: Adding an Initial Cancel-Lock Header Field to a Proto-Article
requirements.text: If the poster or posting agent doesn't add a Cancel-Lock header field to a proto-article, then an injecting agent (or moderator) MAY add one, including one or more <c-lock> elements.

requirements.heading: Adding an Initial Cancel-Lock Header Field to a Proto-Article
requirements.text: If multiple <c-lock> elements are added to the Cancel-Lock header field by a single agent, each <c-lock> element MUST use a unique key "K" to improve security.

requirements.heading: Adding an Initial Cancel-Lock Header Field to a Proto-Article
requirements.text: If an injecting agent (or moderator) wants to act as a representative for a posting agent without support for the authentication system described in this document, then it MUST be able to positively authenticate the poster and MUST be able to automatically add a working Cancel-Key header field for all proto-articles with cancelling or superseding attempts from that poster.

requirements.heading: Adding an Initial Cancel-Lock Header Field to a Proto-Article
requirements.text: Other agents MUST NOT add this header field to articles or proto-articles that they process.

requirements.heading: Extending the Cancel-Lock Header Field of a Proto-Article
requirements.text: If a Cancel-Lock header field has already been added to a proto-article, then any agent further processing the proto-article up to the injecting agent (inclusively) MAY append additional <c-lock> elements to those already in the header field body.

requirements.heading: Extending the Cancel-Lock Header Field of a Proto-Article
requirements.text: If multiple <c-lock> elements are appended to the Cancel-Lock header field by a single agent, each <c-lock> element MUST use a unique key "K" to improve security.

requirements.heading: Extending the Cancel-Lock Header Field of a Proto-Article
requirements.text: Once an article is injected, then this header field MUST NOT be altered.

requirements.heading: Extending the Cancel-Lock Header Field of a Proto-Article
requirements.text: In particular, relaying agents beyond the injecting agent MUST NOT alter it.

requirements.heading: Adding a Cancel-Key Header Field to a Proto-Article
requirements.text: A Cancel-Key header field MAY be added to a proto-article containing a Control or Supersedes header field by the poster or posting agent and will include one or more <c-key> elements.

requirements.heading: Adding a Cancel-Key Header Field to a Proto-Article
requirements.text: If, as mentioned in Section 3.1, an injecting agent or moderator (acting as a representative for the posting agent) has added a Cancel-Lock header field to an article listed in the Control (with a "cancel" command as defined in [RFC5537]) or Supersedes header field, then (given that it authenticates the poster as being the same as the poster of the original article) it MUST add the Cancel-Key header field with at least one <c-key> element that corresponds to that article.

requirements.heading: Adding a Cancel-Key Header Field to a Proto-Article
requirements.text: Other agents MUST NOT alter this header field.

requirements.heading: Extending the Cancel-Key Header Field of a Proto-Article
requirements.text: If a Cancel-Key header field has already been added to a proto-article, then any agent further processing the proto-article up to the injecting agent (inclusively) MAY append additional <c-key> elements to those already in the header field body.

requirements.heading: Extending the Cancel-Key Header Field of a Proto-Article
requirements.text: If, as mentioned in Section 3.2, an injecting agent or moderator (acting as a representative for the posting agent) has extended the Cancel-Lock header field in an article listed in the Control (with a "cancel" command as defined in [RFC5537]) or Supersedes header field, then (given that it authenticates the poster as being the same as the poster of the original article) it MUST extend the Cancel-Key header field body with at least one <c-key> element that corresponds to that article.

requirements.heading: Calculating the Key Data
requirements.text: The following algorithm is RECOMMENDED to calculate the key "K" based on a local secret <sec>.

requirements.heading: Obsolete Syntax
requirements.text: The following value for <scheme> is now deprecated and SHOULD NOT be generated anymore.

requirements.heading: Obsolete Syntax
requirements.text: Serving agents SHOULD still accept it for a transition period as long as the corresponding hash function is not considered unsafe (see Section 7 for details) or already marked as OBSOLETE in the "Netnews Cancel-Lock Hash Algorithms" registry (Section 8.3).

requirements.heading: Obsolete Syntax
requirements.text: <obs-c-key-string> SHOULD NOT be generated but MUST be accepted.

requirements.heading: Change Control
requirements.text: Netnews Cancel-Lock hash algorithm registrations MUST NOT be deleted.
